Speaking in Tehran on October 4, Araghchi said Iran remains ready to pursue what he called a “just and honourable solution” through diplomacy to end the war. He also highlighted recent meetings with neighbouring countries, particularly Gulf states, describing them as productive and friendly. Araghchi said Iran and its neighbours have begun a new trust-building process aimed at establishing peace, stability and security in the Persian Gulf through regional cooperation.

articles.title: Iran’s revenge strike is locked and loaded? Europe’s biggest American bases are in the crosshairs
articles.description: Fresh intelligence warnings have raised concerns over potential Iranian-linked attacks on U.S. military bases in Europe. According to reports, Israel warned Germany about possible threats to the Spangdahlem and Ramstein air bases, while RAF Fairford in Britain was also identified as a potential target. U.S. intelligence agencies and Western allies reportedly shared warnings with American military leaders in September. Classified assessments suggested drones could be used in any subsequent attacks. The warnings come amid heightened tensions involving Iran, Israel, Russia and the U.S. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had previously warned over the use of British bases for strikes against Iranian territory.

articles.title: Merz arrives in Kyiv with aid; back home, his party hits a new low as Germans back pro-Russia AfD
articles.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv with fresh military and energy support for Ukraine as a new INSA poll showed his CDU/CSU alliance falling to a record-low 18 percent, while the AfD climbed to 30 percent. Merz was expected to announce €1 billion in military aid and advance a joint drone-production agreement during the visit. The trip came after major CDU setbacks in eastern Germany, where the AfD recorded strong results in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Merz continued to defend support for Ukraine and higher defence spending, while warning of alleged Russian hybrid attacks across Europe. Moscow dismissed Berlin’s claims as “nonsense.”

articles.title: Kim oversees 1,000-km hypersonic missile test as Pyongyang claims Seoul, Tokyo failed to track it
articles.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw a reported intermediate-range missile test as Pyongyang showcased what it described as a hypersonic strategic weapons system. North Korea’s KCNA said the missile was launched on October 3 and struck a target about 1,000 kilometres away in the sea, while South Korea said it detected a ballistic missile that flew more than 700 kilometres toward the East Sea. Kim Yo Jong claimed South Korea and Japan failed to fully track the missile, citing what Pyongyang described as a “wave-like trajectory mode.” The test came amid heightened tensions on the Korean Peninsula, while U.S. President Donald Trump highlighted his ties with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
